action_items: FOCUS BUG (still broken): The ScrollView+sibling rewrite did not fix the blur. Most likely cause: ScrollView in react-native-web reconciles its direct children by index, and when displayItems length changes the indices of header-fragment children shift relative to item children, causing react-native-web to remount the TextInput. Two suggested fixes (try in order): (a) wrap renderHeader() output in a single stable <View> so ScrollView's direct child array is [headerView, ...itemViews] and header stays at index 0 regardless of items length; (b) hoist ListFilterBar out of the ScrollView entirely so it lives as a sibling of ScrollView under the SafeAreaView (this is the cleanest fix — Shared tab works because its FlatList ListHeaderComponent is functionally hoisted by FlatList itself; in ScrollView you need to do it manually). Also memoize ListFilterBar with React.memo and stabilize the setSearch/setDateRange/setDecisionType callbacks with useCallback to avoid prop-identity churn.

critical_code_review_comments: /app/frontend/app/(tabs)/prr.tsx line 474: renderHeader() returns a React Fragment with 3-4 children. Recommend wrapping its output in a single <View> so the ScrollView sees a stable [header, ...items] child array (prevents react-native-web from re-keying TextInput when items length changes).

/app/frontend/src/components/ListFilterBar.tsx: Not wrapped in React.memo and onChangeText/onSearch callbacks are passed as fresh arrow-function/prop instances each render. Combined with the parent re-render on each keystroke this can amplify reconciliation cost and increases the chance of focus loss in react-native-web.

/app/frontend/app/(tabs)/prr.tsx contentContainerStyle on ScrollView passes a fresh array literal each render ({styles.list, { paddingBottom: 100 }}). Extract to a constant or memoize to avoid prop identity churn.

rca_of_issue: Focus loss RCA hypothesis: In /app/frontend/app/(tabs)/prr.tsx the ScrollView's direct children are `renderHeader()` (a Fragment containing folder grid, filter row, type chips, and ListFilterBar) followed by `displayItems.map(...)` items. React flattens the Fragment children into the parent ScrollView's child list, so the ScrollView effectively has [folder, filterRow, typeChips, ListFilterBar, item0, item1, ...]. When the user types the first key, search state changes, displayItems is recomputed by useMemo and may change length/identity, which shifts every subsequent index. react-native-web's ScrollView (a div with overflow:auto) reconciles its DOM children by index and will commit a structural diff that, in practice, causes the inner <input> inside ListFilterBar to be detached/reattached, dropping focus. The Shared tab does not exhibit this because FlatList's ListHeaderComponent is rendered in a stable wrapper independent of the data list. Recommended mitigation: wrap renderHeader() in a single <View>, OR hoist ListFilterBar to be a sibling of (not inside) the ScrollView.
